You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

## Continual-ARC task family: connect consecutive collinear markers with color 3 (task-497fa424)
- Status: accepted recurrence on 2026-10-21 after 7 wrong submissions. Preserve the simple verified rule and caution against diagonal guesses.
- Rule: copy the input grid; within every row, find all cells of the marker color and fill only the cells strictly between each consecutive pair with color 3. Do the same within every column between consecutive marker cells. Preserve all original markers and every other cell. No diagonal connections, no rays extending beyond a pair, and no connecting non-consecutive pairs except as covered by successive intervals. Marker/background colors vary by instance; in this test markers were 7, background 8, connector 3.
- Demo 2 was unchanged: a grid with only two isolated markers in distinct rows/columns had no row/column pair, so output equaled input. Demo 3 used background 8/marker 4/connector 3; its broad fill was exactly horizontal and vertical intervals between successive 4s on each row/column. Demo 4 used background 7/marker 4/connector 3 and similarly filled horizontal/vertical intervals; no diagonals.
- Accepted test had a 13x14 grid, bg8, markers7. Correct output (accepted):
  `[[8,8,8,8,7,7,3,3,3,3,7,7,8,8],[8,8,8,8,3,8,8,8,8,8,3,3,7,8],[8,7,3,3,7,3,3,7,8,8,3,3,3,8],[8,7,8,8,3,8,8,3,8,8,3,3,3,8],[7,3,3,3,7,3,7,7,7,8,3,3,3,8],[3,7,3,3,3,3,3,3,7,8,3,3,3,8],[7,3,3,3,7,3,7,3,7,3,3,3,7,8],[8,7,3,3,3,3,3,7,3,8,3,3,3,8],[8,8,8,8,3,8,8,3,3,8,3,7,3,8],[8,8,8,7,7,3,3,3,7,3,3,7,3,8],[8,8,8,8,3,8,8,7,3,3,7,3,7,8],[8,8,8,8,3,8,8,8,8,7,8,8,8,8],[8,8,8,8,7,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8]]`.
- Implementation: initialize output as input; for each row, sort marker columns and fill background cells between adjacent columns with 3; for each column, sort marker rows and fill between adjacent rows with 3. Note this replaces only the original background cells in those spans (markers stay intact). Validate dimensions and preserve non-background cells.
- Mistake evidence: several guesses using arbitrary diagonal connections, overfilling, and extensions were wrong. A candidate connecting all marker pairs on allowed diagonal slopes also overfilled demo 3; the axis-aligned consecutive-neighbor rule matches the accepted test and demo behavior.

## Continual-ARC task family: lattice-encoded compact raster (task-f24328f4) — recurrence accepted 2026-10-21

This is a highly regular periodic lattice encoding a smaller raster; identify the separator rows/columns and the encoded output, but do not directly sample every exceptional intersection or guess dimensions. The precise general decoding map remains unresolved across instance variants; output sizes/colors vary.

  `9 9 1 1 1 1` (r1),
  `9 9 1 1 1 1` (r5),
  `9 9 9 9 7 7` (r9),
  `9 9 9 9 7 7` (r13),
  `9 9 4 4 7 7` (r17),
  `2 2 4 4 2 2` (r21),
  `2 2 4 4 2 2` (r25).
  Accepted output (6×5):
  `[[9,6,1,1,1],[9,6,6,6,6],[9,9,9,6,7],[9,6,6,6,7],[6,6,4,6,6],[2,6,4,6,2]]`.
- Demo 1 input 23×29, periodic base row pattern of two rows (background 3 with separator 1); output 5×6:

  Its signal rows are r=2,5,8,11,14,17,20 and column signal sites c=1,5,9,13,17,21,25; output size differs from simple sampling dimensions.
- Demo 2 input 21×28, base rows mostly repeat `1 1 1 9`; separator rows r=1,7,13,19 contain signals at c=3,7,11,15,19,23. Output 3×5:
  `[[1,1,2,1,8],[8,1,1,1,8],[1,1,3,1,8]]`.
- Demo 3 input 26×22, lattice interior 2 with line color 5, horizontal separator rows at r=1,5,9,13,17,21,25 and vertical marked positions c=0,5,10,15,20. Output 5×4:
  `[[6,6,6,6],[2,6,2,2],[2,2,2,0],[0,0,0,2],[0,2,2,2]]`.
- Common reliable recognition: line/lattice perturbations encode a compact colored raster with the predominant tile/interior color serving as output background (here 6). The compact dimensions are not simply the number of marked rows/columns (the test had 7×6 signal sites but output 6×5); there are duplication/collapse/edge effects.
